scenario: At which OSI layer do routers make forwarding decisions based on IP addresses?
explanation: OSI layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

scenario: At which OSI layer do switches forward frames using MAC addresses?
explanation: Data at Layer 2 is called a frame; at Layer 3, a packet.

scenario: What is the data unit called at the Transport layer when using TCP?
explanation: With UDP, the unit is often called a datagram.

scenario: Which TCP/IP model layer maps to OSI layers 5, 6 and 7?
explanation: The TCP/IP model has four layers: Network Access (Link), Internet, Transport, Application.

scenario: What's the difference between bandwidth and throughput?

options.text: Bandwidth is capacity; throughput is actual data delivered
They always have the same value on a healthy network
Throughput is the maximum capacity of the link

explanation: Latency, congestion and errors reduce throughput below bandwidth.

scenario: Which tool measures throughput between two endpoints you control, rather than to an internet server?
explanation: iPerf runs as a client and server to measure throughput across your own network.

scenario: Which network type covers a single building or office?
explanation: A WLAN is a wireless LAN; a CAN covers a campus of buildings.

scenario: Which network type connects Bluetooth earbuds and a phone around one person?
explanation: Personal area networks have a range of a few meters.

scenario: Which physical topology connects every device to a central switch?

options.note: Every device linked to every other.

explanation: Star is the most common topology for Ethernet LANs.

scenario: Which cloud service model gives you virtual machines and networks to manage yourself?
explanation: With IaaS, you manage the OS and apps; the provider manages hardware.

scenario: Which protocol is connection-oriented and guarantees delivery with acknowledgments?
explanation: TCP uses a three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

scenario: Which transport protocol is best for live video calls where speed matters more than retransmission?
explanation: DNS queries and VoIP also commonly use UDP.

scenario: Which protocol and port does HTTPS use by default?
explanation: HTTPS encrypts HTTP with TLS.

scenario: Which protocol securely transfers files over an SSH connection?
explanation: SFTP uses TCP port 22.

scenario: Which protocol is used by devices to sync their clocks?
explanation: Accurate time matters for logs and authentication.

scenario: Which protocol does ping use to test reachability?
explanation: Ping sends ICMP echo requests and waits for echo replies.

scenario: Which IPv4 address is a private address?
What does NAT do on a home router?

options.text: Translates private addresses to a public address
Encrypts all Wi-Fi traffic between devices
Blocks every inbound port from the internet

explanation: PAT (NAT overload) lets many devices share one public IP using different ports.

scenario: What is the subnet mask for a /24 network?
explanation: A /24 has 24 network bits and 8 host bits.

scenario: How many usable host addresses are in a /24 subnet?
explanation: Usable hosts = 2^host bits − 2.

scenario: What is the broadcast address of 192.168.10.0/24?
explanation: The broadcast address has all host bits set to 1.

scenario: How many usable hosts are in a /26 subnet?
explanation: /26 leaves 6 host bits: 2^6 − 2 = 62.

scenario: Which subnet mask matches /27?
Which address class has a default mask of 255.255.0.0?
explanation: Class B first octets range from 128 to 191.

scenario: A Windows PC has the address 169.254.20.15. What does this mean?

options.text: It couldn't reach a DHCP server
It has a valid, routable public internet address

explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is APIPA (link-local); check the cable and DHCP server.

scenario: How long is an IPv6 address?
explanation: IPv6 addresses are written as eight groups of four hex digits.

scenario: Which is the correct shortened form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001?
explanation: Drop leading zeros in each group; replace one run of zero groups with ::.

scenario: Which IPv6 address type begins with fe80 and works only on the local link?
explanation: Every IPv6 interface automatically gets a link-local address.

scenario: What is the IPv6 loopback address?
explanation: Ping ::1 to test the local IPv6 stack.

scenario: What is the typical prefix length for an IPv6 subnet on a LAN?
explanation: The first 64 bits identify the network; the last 64 bits identify the interface.

scenario: Which device separates broadcast domains?
explanation: VLANs also separate broadcast domains on a switch.

scenario: Which connector is used on standard twisted-pair Ethernet cables?
explanation: Cat 5e, Cat 6 and Cat 6a cables use RJ-45 connectors.

scenario: What is the maximum recommended length of a copper Ethernet cable run?
explanation: Longer runs need a switch or fiber.

scenario: Which cable type is immune to electromagnetic interference and supports long distances?
explanation: Single-mode fiber reaches farther than multimode.

scenario: Which fiber type uses a narrow core and lasers for very long distances?
explanation: Multimode is common inside buildings and data centers.

scenario: Which fiber connector is small, with a push-pull latch, and common on SFP modules?
explanation: SC is a larger square push-pull connector.

scenario: Which Wi-Fi band offers the longest range but more interference?
explanation: Microwaves and Bluetooth also use 2.4 GHz.

scenario: Which Wi-Fi standard added support for the 6 GHz band?
explanation: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) also uses 6 GHz.

scenario: Which is a common source of interference for 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi?
explanation: Cordless phones, Bluetooth and thick walls also affect signal.

scenario: Which wireless setting is the network name users see when connecting?
explanation: Hiding the SSID is not a real security control.

scenario: A laptop shows the Wi-Fi network but fails to connect with an authentication error. What should be checked first?

options.text: The Wi-Fi password and security type
The DNS server address in the IP settings

explanation: Mismatched WPA2/WPA3 settings can also prevent connection.

scenario: Which command shows IP settings on a Linux computer?
explanation: ifconfig also works on many Linux and macOS systems.

scenario: Where do you check Wi-Fi and IP settings on an iPhone?

options.text: Settings > Wi-Fi > the network's info icon
Control Panel > Network and Sharing Center
Terminal app with the ipconfig command

explanation: Android shows similar details under Network and internet.

scenario: Which endpoint is an IoT device?
explanation: IoT devices are often on separate VLANs for security.

scenario: Which cellular technology provides the highest speeds and lowest latency today?
explanation: Cellular is often used as a backup WAN link.

scenario: What does PoE allow a switch port to do?

options.text: Provide power over the Ethernet cable
Encrypt all traffic leaving the port
Connect fiber cables without an SFP

explanation: PoE powers IP phones, cameras and access points.

scenario: A switch port's link light is off after a cable is connected. What does this usually mean?

options.text: The device has an IP conflict

explanation: Check the cable, the device's NIC and whether the port is shut down.

scenario: On many Cisco switches, what does a blinking green port LED indicate?

options.text: Traffic is passing on the link
The port is in power-saving mode

explanation: Solid green means link up with no activity; amber can mean blocked or faulty.

scenario: Which port is used to configure a new Cisco switch with no IP address yet?
explanation: Use a console (rollover or USB) cable and a terminal emulator.

scenario: Which pluggable module lets a switch port use fiber or different speeds?
explanation: SFP+ supports 10 Gbps; QSFP supports higher speeds.

scenario: What is the default gateway?

options.text: The router that sends traffic to other networks
The switch that connects local PCs
The DNS server for name lookups
The DHCP server that hands out addresses

explanation: Devices send traffic for remote networks to their default gateway.

scenario: A PC can reach devices on its own subnet but not the internet. What's a likely cause?

options.text: The wrong MAC address on the PC
An expired DHCP lease on the switch
options.note: Switches do not hold client leases.

explanation: Verify the gateway with ipconfig and ping it.

scenario: What's the main difference between a Layer 2 switch and a Layer 3 switch?

options.text: A Layer 3 switch can also route between VLANs
A Layer 2 switch uses IP addresses
A Layer 3 switch can't use VLANs or trunks
They're identical except for the number of ports

explanation: Layer 3 switches use switched virtual interfaces (SVIs) to route.

scenario: How does a switch learn which device is connected to each port?
explanation: Entries are stored in the MAC address table (CAM table).

scenario: What does a switch do with a frame whose destination MAC isn't in its table?

options.text: Floods it out all ports except the one it came in on
Drops it immediately to protect the network
Sends it back to the sender
Sends it only to the default gateway port

explanation: When the destination replies, the switch learns its port.

scenario: What does a VLAN do?

options.text: Divides one switch into separate broadcast domains
Increases the speed of each switch port
Provides Wi-Fi access to guest devices

explanation: Trunks carry multiple VLANs between switches using 802.1Q tags.

scenario: Which switch port type carries traffic for multiple VLANs to another switch?
explanation: 802.1Q adds a VLAN tag to frames on trunks.

scenario: Which security feature limits which MAC addresses can use a switch port?
explanation: Violations can shut down the port.

scenario: Following a network diagram, which device should a PC's patch cable connect to?
explanation: Patch panels connect building cabling to switches in the rack.

scenario: Which device is usually at the edge of a small office network connecting it to the ISP?
explanation: Small business routers often include firewall and VPN features.

scenario: What does a Cisco router use to decide where to send a packet?
explanation: Routes can be connected, static or learned by dynamic protocols like OSPF.

scenario: Which command shows the IP address, subnet mask and default gateway on Windows?
explanation: Use ipconfig /all for DNS servers and MAC addresses.

scenario: Which command shows each router hop to a destination on Windows?
explanation: Linux and macOS use traceroute.

scenario: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but can't open websites by name. What's the most likely problem?
explanation: Use nslookup to test DNS.

scenario: Why might ping fail to a server that's actually up and serving web pages?

options.text: The server has no MAC address
Web servers can't reply to ping

explanation: Many firewalls block ICMP echo requests by default.

scenario: Which tool captures packets so you can inspect the protocols on a network?
explanation: Captures are saved as .pcap or .pcapng files.

scenario: Which Cisco command shows the full current configuration?
explanation: show startup-config shows the saved configuration.

scenario: Which Cisco command lists directly connected Cisco devices?
explanation: CDP is Cisco Discovery Protocol; LLDP is the vendor-neutral equivalent.

scenario: Which Cisco command quickly shows interface IP addresses and up/down status?
explanation: Status 'administratively down' means the interface was shut down.

scenario: In Cisco IOS, which prompt indicates privileged EXEC mode?
explanation: Type enable to move from user EXEC to privileged EXEC.

scenario: What does typing ? at a Cisco IOS prompt do?
explanation: Context-sensitive help works mid-command too.

scenario: Which protocol provides encrypted command-line access to a network device?
explanation: Disable Telnet and use SSH for remote management.

scenario: Which cloud-managed platform lets admins manage Cisco networks from a web dashboard?
explanation: Meraki devices are configured and monitored from the cloud.

scenario: What's the first step in a structured troubleshooting process?

options.text: Gather information and identify the problem
Replace the switch that's closest to the user
Reboot every device in the network

explanation: Then establish a theory, test it, plan, implement, verify and document.

scenario: Which ticket should usually be handled first?

options.text: A whole office can't access the network
One user wants a new mouse
A request to rename a printer
A question about a password policy

explanation: Priority is based on impact and urgency.

scenario: Which tool is a terminal emulator used for console or SSH connections?
explanation: Tera Term and SecureCRT are other examples.

scenario: A firewall rule denies TCP port 3389 inbound. What service is blocked?
explanation: Blocking unneeded ports reduces the attack surface.

scenario: How are firewall rules usually processed?

options.text: Top to bottom until the first match
All rules are applied together at the same time
Bottom to top, with the last match winning

explanation: Most firewalls end with an implicit deny-all rule.

scenario: Which AAA component records what a user did after logging in?
explanation: RADIUS and TACACS+ are common AAA protocols.

scenario: Which is an example of multifactor authentication?

options.text: A password plus a phone app code

explanation: Factors: something you know, have, or are.

scenario: What does a digital certificate prove on an HTTPS website?

options.text: The site's identity, signed by a trusted CA
The site has been scanned and contains no malware
The user's password meets the site's rules

explanation: Browsers warn when certificates are expired or untrusted.

scenario: Which home router wireless security option should you choose for the best protection?
explanation: Use WPA2-AES if older devices don't support WPA3.

scenario: What's the difference between WPA2-Personal and WPA2-Enterprise?

options.text: Enterprise uses individual logins through a RADIUS server
Personal uses stronger encryption than Enterprise
Enterprise has no password, only MAC filtering

explanation: Personal uses one pre-shared key for everyone.

scenario: Which directory service stores user accounts and groups in many Windows organizations?
explanation: Identity stores centralize authentication.

scenario: Which threat floods a server with traffic to make it unavailable?
explanation: A DDoS uses many attacking systems at once.

scenario: Which threat tricks users into clicking a malicious link in an email?
explanation: Verify senders and hover over links before clicking.

scenario: Which part of the CIA triad does encryption mainly protect?
explanation: Hashing supports integrity; redundancy supports availability.

scenario: Which password policy best improves security?

options.text: Require long passphrases and block common passwords
Require users to change passwords every day

explanation: Length and uniqueness matter more than frequent changes.

scenario: Which change should you make first on a new home router?

options.text: Turn on WEP for older devices
Open all ports for gaming consoles

explanation: Also update the firmware and use WPA3 or WPA2.

scenario: Which firewall action silently discards traffic without notifying the sender?

options.note: Sends a response like ICMP unreachable.

explanation: Deny rules can be configured to drop or reject.

scenario: What is malware?

options.text: Software designed to harm or exploit systems
A slow or unstable internet connection
A firewall rule that blocks applications

explanation: Types include viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware and spyware.
